exercises.name: March
exercises.purpose: For keeping up on family walks
tips: Stand or sit tall, eyes ahead
Lift one foot, set it down softly
Arms swing, or hands rest on thighs
exercises.easier: Just lift your heels, toes stay down
exercises.harder: Knees a little higher, arms press forward

limitNotes.text: Keep your knees well below your hips

exercises.name: Heel dig
tips: Heel down in front, toes up
Bring the foot back, then switch
Upper body stays tall and still
exercises.easier: Slow it down, same small reach
exercises.harder: Switch feet a little quicker

exercises.name: Side step
tips: Step out to the side, then together
Knees soft, toes point forward
Hips stay level, eyes ahead
exercises.easier: Small steps, hands on your hips
exercises.harder: Wider steps, arms open to the sides

limitNotes.text: Small steps, close to your chair

exercises.name: Knee lift
tips: Hold the chair or seat lightly
Knee no higher than your hip
Foot points forward, body tall
exercises.easier: Lift lower, hand on the chair
exercises.harder: Touch the knee with the opposite hand

limitNotes.text: Knees stay clearly below your hips

exercises.name: Toe tap forward
tips: Tap your toes out in front
Knee stays a little bent
Stay tall, don't lean back
exercises.easier: Tap a little closer to you
exercises.harder: A low kick, knee never locked

exercises.name: Heel to back
tips: Hold the chair, stand tall
Bring your heel back and up
Knee points down, don't lean forward
exercises.easier: Lift your heel only a little
exercises.harder: Hands off the chair, if you feel steady

limitNotes.text: Bend only as far as feels comfortable

exercises.name: Weight shift
tips: Feet a little wider than your hips
Shift your weight side to side
Knees stay over your toes
exercises.easier: Hold the chair as you shift
exercises.harder: Let the other heel lift a little

exercises.name: Arm swing / press
tips: Swing your arms, elbows soft
Or press forward at shoulder height
Shoulders stay down and relaxed
exercises.easier: Keep your hands below your shoulders
exercises.harder: Press up and out at an angle

limitNotes.text: Keep your hands below shoulder height

exercises.name: Sit-to-stand
tips: Feet flat, hip-width apart
Lean forward, nose over toes
Use your hands on the chair if you need to
exercises.easier: Push up with your hands on the chair
exercises.harder: Arms crossed, sit down on a slow count of three

exercises.name: Seated knee lift
tips: Hold the sides of your seat
Sit tall, don't lean back
Lift, then set down softly
exercises.easier: Just lift your heel, toes stay down
exercises.harder: Lift a little higher and swing the opposite arm

exercises.name: Seated leg extension
tips: Hold the sides of your seat
Leg points straight ahead
Lower it slowly
exercises.easier: Straighten your leg only halfway
exercises.harder: Hold it up for a count of three

exercises.name: Heel and toe raises
tips: Feet flat to start
Lift heels, then lower
Now lift toes, heels stay down
exercises.easier: Heels only, small lifts
exercises.harder: Stand behind your chair and rise onto your toes

exercises.name: Wall push-up
exercises.purpose: For pushing doors and lifting bags
tips: Hands flat at shoulder height
Body straight, like a plank
Heels stay on the floor
exercises.easier: Stand closer, bend your elbows just a bit
exercises.harder: Step your feet back a little

exercises.name: Single-leg stand
tips: Hold the chair with both hands
Look at one spot ahead
Lift your foot just a little
exercises.easier: Lift only your heel, toes stay down
exercises.harder: Hold on with just one hand

exercises.name: Side leg raise
exercises.purpose: For getting out of the car
tips: Hold the chair back with both hands
Lift about a hand's height, toes forward
Stay tall, no leaning to the side
exercises.easier: A smaller lift, both hands on the chair
exercises.harder: Hold on with just one hand

limitNotes.text: A small lift, toes and knee face forward

exercises.name: Back leg raise
tips: Stand tall, hands on the chair
Leg moves straight back, toes down
Don't lean forward or arch your back
exercises.easier: A smaller lift, just off the floor
exercises.harder: Pause at the top for a moment

limitNotes.text: A small lift, no arching your back

exercises.name: Knee curl
tips: Hands on the chair, stand tall
Bring your heel up behind you
Knee points down, thigh stays still
exercises.easier: Bend your knee only a little
exercises.harder: Hands off the chair, if you feel steady

limitNotes.text: Bend only as far as feels comfortable

exercises.name: Mini-squat
tips: Both hands on the chair, feet hip-width
Sit back a little, heels stay down
Knees point forward, not past your toes
exercises.easier: Just a small bend at the knees
exercises.harder: Lower on a slow count of three

limitNotes.text: Halfway only, stop if your heels lift

exercises.name: Arm raises
tips: Sit tall, feet flat
Raise your arms to shoulder height
Elbows soft, shoulders stay down
exercises.easier: Lift only partway, below your shoulders
exercises.harder: Pause at the top, or reach overhead

exercises.name: Seated row
tips: Arms out in front, palms facing in
Pull your elbows back past your ribs
Squeeze your shoulder blades together
exercises.easier: Pull back only halfway
exercises.harder: Hold the squeeze for a count of two

exercises.name: Neck turn
tips: Chin level, shoulders down
Only as far as is comfortable
exercises.easier: Turn halfway, eyes open, move slowly

exercises.name: Side of the neck
tips: Hand on the opposite shoulder
Ear toward shoulder, no pulling
exercises.easier: Tilt a little, skip the hand on the shoulder

exercises.name: Chin tuck
exercises.purpose: For after reading or screen time
tips: Glide your head straight back
Eyes level, don't look up
exercises.easier: A smaller glide, just a few times

exercises.name: Shoulder rolls
exercises.purpose: For shoulders after a busy day
tips: Roll up, back, then down, slowly
Head still, hands on your thighs
exercises.easier: Make the circles smaller

exercises.name: Chest and shoulders
tips: Shoulders back and down
Chest forward and up, gently
exercises.easier: Hands resting on your hips instead of arms out

exercises.name: Upper back reach
tips: Arms forward, palms facing away
Reach forward, lower back stays tall
exercises.easier: Keep your hands a little lower

limitNotes.text: Back stays straight, just reach your arms

exercises.name: Upper back twist
exercises.purpose: For turning to reach for things
tips: Arms crossed, hands on shoulders
Turn from the chest, hips stay still
exercises.easier: Turn a small way, head in line with your body

exercises.name: Side stretch
tips: Sit tall, feet flat
Reach up and over, or slide your hand down
exercises.easier: Arm by your side, lean a little

exercises.name: Back of the thigh
tips: Heel down, toes up
Lean forward from the hips, back long
exercises.easier: Keep the knee a little bent, lean only a little

exercises.name: Ankle circles and points
tips: Hold the side of the seat
Point your toes away, then back
exercises.easier: Keep your heel on the floor, just lift and lower your toes

exercises.name: Calf stretch
tips: Both feet flat, back heel down
Hold the chair the whole time
exercises.easier: Shorter step back, back knee a little bent

exercises.name: Overhead reach at the wall
tips: Walk your hands up the wall
Heels down, don't arch your back
exercises.easier: Stop when your hands reach eye level

limitNotes.text: Sit tall and reach up instead

exercises.name: Tandem stance
tips: Hold the chair the whole time
Front heel touches your back toes
Knees soft, eyes straight ahead
exercises.easier: Front foot a little to the side
exercises.harder: Just your fingertips on the chair

limitNotes.text: Feet stay in line, never crossing over

exercises.name: Sideways walking
tips: Step to the side, feet together
Toes point forward, hips level
Stay near a counter or wall
exercises.easier: Smaller steps, one hand on the counter
exercises.harder: Slightly bigger steps, same slow pace

limitNotes.text: Small steps, one hand on the counter

exercises.name: Heel-to-toe walk
tips: Fingertips on the wall beside you
Heel lands right in front of toes
Eyes ahead, one slow step at a time
exercises.easier: Leave a small gap between steps
exercises.harder: A few more steps, same slow pace
